page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is an x86_64 GPU-accelerated compute instance featuring a dedicated 4-core, 8-thread Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with a 40 MB L3 cache. It provides 60.0 GB of system RAM (7.5 GB per vCPU), a 472 GB local SSD volume, and a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single bundled NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark data reflects clear architectural contrasts between host CPU throughput and GPU execution capabilities. The Broadwell-generation Intel Xeon CPU produces modest results, falling into lower benchmark percentiles for stress-ng compute tasks (954.2 single-core, 4765.11 multi-core) and PassMark CPU subtests. The instruction set supports standard AVX, AES, and FMA extensions, but lacks newer AVX-512 and AMX vector capabilities. Memory read bandwidth tests and compression workloads also post lower-tier performance scores.

In contrast, the integrated NVIDIA P100 GPU delivers notable acceleration for machine learning workloads that fit within its 16 GB memory boundary. Benchmarks indicate top-tier prompt processing throughput across small models (9872.83 tokens/sec on 135M) and medium models (316.69 tokens/sec on 7B), accompanied by strong text generation speeds (42.77 tokens/sec on 7B). However, lack of sufficient VRAM precludes running larger 70B parameter models.

Cost efficiency is centered around legacy GPU acceleration. While its host processor and memory subsystem offer reduced performance relative to newer architectures, the server provides cost-effective entry-level GPU processing with local SSD storage for specialized compute-intensive and smaller deep learning tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server equipped with an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor (4 physical cores, 8 vCPUs at 2.5 GHz), 60.0 GB of memory, a 472 GB local SSD, and 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The hardware core features a bundled NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB VRAM. Synthetic CPU and system memory benchmarks indicate lower-tier host performance, characterized by modest stress-ng and compression results alongside standard AVX vector support. However, GPU inference benchmarks demonstrate high-tier prompt processing for small and medium-sized language models (9872.83 tokens/sec on a 135M model and 316.69 tokens/sec on a 7B model). With its combined local storage and dedicated Pascal accelerator, this instance provides cost-effective throughput for GPU-assisted mathematical computing, legacy deep learning development, and medium model inference pipelines where advanced host CPU capabilities are not strictly required.
